subject.title: [Bug]: Windows Scheduled Task gateway restart/health becomes inconsistent after ready

question: Should #63491 remain the broad canonical Windows Scheduled Task restart/health tracker pending live Windows proof, or should the remaining work be split entirely into narrower schtasks issues?
rationale: Current main and the latest release fix two reported subsets, but source and related issue evidence show remaining daemon fallback/relaunch gaps and no merged PR covers the full post-ready health report.

options.title: Keep broad tracker open
options.body: Keep #63491 open as the umbrella until live Windows proof demonstrates the full Scheduled Task restart, fallback, listener ownership, cron recovery, and post-ready health path.

options.title: Split into narrow issues
options.body: Close this only after maintainers explicitly confirm the broader post-ready health context is fully represented by narrower open issues such as #90158 and #91144.

options.title: Require fresh reporter repro first
options.body: Pause implementation until a maintainer or reporter provides current-release Windows logs proving the post-ready HTTP/port-loss symptom still reproduces outside the known schtasks subsets.

recommendation.title: Keep broad tracker open
recommendation.body: Keep #63491 open as the umbrella until live Windows proof demonstrates the full Scheduled Task restart, fallback, listener ownership, cron recovery, and post-ready health path.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is assigned to vincentkoc and his recent policy-close work already resolved one subset of the report.
